gloss: plant division (horticulture); dividing a plant at the root

definitions.gloss: dividing a plant at the root; plant division; root division
definitions.explanation: A method of propagating plants by digging up an established clump and splitting its root mass into two or more sections, each of which is replanted as a new individual. Used for many perennials, grasses, and houseplants that grow in clumps.

examples.japanese: {株分|かぶわ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To divide a plant at the root.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{株分|かぶわ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{育|そだ}つ→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧。
examples.english: If you divide it in spring, the plant will grow vigorously.
My mother divided the flowers in the garden and gave some to the neighbors.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧アロエ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{株分|かぶわ}け⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{簡単|かんたん}→簡単：00713_kantan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{増|ふ}やせる→増やす：02410_fuyasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{初心者|しょしんしゃ}→初心者：10149_shoshinsha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦おすすめ→おすすめ：09746_osusume⟧だ。
examples.english: This aloe can be easily propagated by division, so it's recommended even for beginners.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{株|かぶ}→株：02592_kabu⟧ (the root or base of a plant; a clump) + {分|わ}け (division, from the verb ⟦{分|わ}ける→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧ to divide). A standard method of plant propagation in which an overgrown clump is carefully dug up and split at the roots into several smaller plants.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {株分|かぶわ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to perform root division
- {株分|かぶわ}け⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{増|ふ}やす→増やす：02410_fuyasu⟧: to propagate by division
- ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{株分|かぶわ}け: spring division
- {株分|かぶわ}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{適|てき}した→適する：02297_tekisuru⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧: the right season for root division

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{挿|さ}し{木|き}→挿し木：08105_sashiki⟧: cutting — propagation by rooting a piece of stem or branch, rather than dividing the root mass.
- {取|と}り{木|き}: layering — propagation by bending a branch down to the soil so it grows its own roots before being separated.
- ⟦{接|つ}ぎ{木|き}→接ぎ木：08106_tsugiki⟧: grafting — joining a shoot of one plant onto the rootstock of another.

USAGE:
A common word in gardening magazines, plant-care guides, and nursery labels. {株分|かぶわ}け is typically recommended for hostas, ornamental grasses, irises, daylilies, ferns, and many succulents. The best time of year depends on the species, but early spring and autumn are most common.
